paragraphs.title: The Prophecy Against the Altar and the Sign

easy.explanation: The verse says that the man of God came out of Judah.
easy.q: Where did the man of God come from?

answers: The altar and the coming of Josiah
easy.explanation: He prophesied against the altar and spoke of Josiah, a future descendant of David.
easy.q: What did the man of God prophesy against?

easy.explanation: Jeroboam's hand dried up when he stretched it out against the man of God.

answers: The altar was rent and the ashes were poured out
medium.explanation: The sign was that the altar was rent and its ashes were poured out.
medium.q: What sign was given that day?

answers: So he could find the way
So that his hand might be restored
So that he might receive food
medium.explanation: Jeroboam asked for prayer so that his dried-up hand would be restored.
medium.q: Why did Jeroboam ask the man of God to pray for him?

medium.explanation: The sign was a miraculous event confirming the word of the Lord.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “sign” mean?

answers: The rent altar was the sign confirming the prophecy
The rent altar canceled the prophecy
The rent altar was punishment for the prophet
challenge.explanation: The altar being rent and the ashes being poured out fulfilled the sign announced by the man of God.
challenge.q: What was the relationship between the prophecy and the altar being rent?

answers: That the prophet sought personal honor
That prayer brought about the restoration of the hand
challenge.explanation: After the man of God prayed, the king's hand was restored and became as it was before.
challenge.q: What did the restoration of Jeroboam's hand show?

answers: He refused and returned by another way
challenge.explanation: He obeyed the Lord's command not to eat or drink there and returned by another way.
challenge.q: What did the man of God do after Jeroboam offered him food and a reward?

paragraphs.title: The Old Prophet Misleads the Man of God

easy.explanation: The passage says that an old prophet dwelt in Bethel.
easy.q: Where did the old prophet live?

easy.explanation: The old prophet's sons told him all that had happened.
easy.q: Who told the old prophet about the works of the man of God?

easy.explanation: He invited the man of God to come home with him and eat bread.
easy.q: What did the old prophet invite the man of God to do?

answers: His sons had seen the way
He found the way written down
medium.explanation: His sons had seen the way taken by the man of God and told him.
medium.q: How did the old prophet know which way the man of God had gone?

answers: He had been commanded not to eat or drink there
He did not know the old prophet
medium.explanation: He explained that the word of the Lord had commanded him not to eat or drink there.
medium.q: Why did the man of God first refuse the old prophet's invitation?

medium.explanation: The old prophet claimed to have received a message from the Lord, but the passage says that he lied.
medium.q: What does “lied unto him” mean in this passage?

answers: The old prophet's claim that an angel had spoken to him
A request from the prophet's sons
challenge.explanation: The old prophet claimed that an angel had instructed him to bring the man of God back.
challenge.q: What caused the man of God to change his decision?

answers: The original command forbade eating and drinking, while the old prophet permitted them
The original command required him to stay, while the old prophet told him to leave
challenge.explanation: The man of God was told not to eat or drink, but the old prophet told him to do so.
challenge.q: What was the difference between the original command and the old prophet's message?

answers: He returned with the old prophet and ate and drank
challenge.explanation: He went back with the old prophet, ate bread, and drank water in his house.
challenge.q: What happened because the man of God believed the old prophet?

paragraphs.title: The Punishment and the Lion Guarding the Body

answers: As they sat at the table
easy.explanation: The word of the Lord came as they sat at the table.
easy.q: When did the word of the Lord come concerning the man of God's punishment?

easy.explanation: A lion met him by the way and slew him.
easy.q: What did the lion do to the man of God?

answers: It left both and ran away
It stood beside the body without harming the donkey
easy.explanation: The lion did not eat the body or tear the donkey.
easy.q: What did the lion do to the body and the donkey?

answers: He disobeyed the word of the Lord and did not keep the commandment
medium.explanation: The prophet declared that he had disobeyed the Lord and failed to keep the commandment.
medium.q: Why was the man of God punished?

answers: It slew the man of God but neither ate him nor harmed the donkey
medium.explanation: The lion slew the man of God but did not eat the body or tear the donkey.
medium.q: What was unusual about the lion's behavior?

medium.explanation: “Carcase” means the body of a person after death.
medium.q: What does “carcase” mean in this passage?

answers: The lion stood by the body while the donkey remained unharmed
challenge.explanation: The lion stood beside the body and the donkey without eating or harming them.
challenge.q: What did the travelers see that made the event extraordinary?

answers: The Lord had delivered him unto the lion
The donkey had caused his death
challenge.explanation: The old prophet said that the Lord had delivered him unto the lion because he was disobedient.
challenge.q: How did the old prophet explain the death of the man of God?

answers: The man died on the way and did not come to the sepulchre of his fathers
The prophecy was canceled because the lion did not eat him
The prophecy concerned only the altar
challenge.explanation: The man of God died on the way, fulfilling the announced judgment that his body would not come to his fathers' sepulchre.
challenge.q: How was the prophecy of punishment fulfilled?

paragraphs.title: The Burial of the Man of God and the Old Prophet's Recognition

easy.explanation: The old prophet took up the body and brought it back to the city.
easy.q: Who brought the body of the man of God back to the city?

answers: In the old prophet's own grave
easy.explanation: The old prophet laid the body in his own grave.
easy.q: Where was the man of God buried?

answers: Bury him beside the bones of the man of God
easy.explanation: He asked that his bones be laid beside the bones of the man of God.
easy.q: What did the old prophet ask his sons to do after his death?

answers: They mourned him and said, “Alas, my brother!”
They asked Jeroboam for a reward
medium.explanation: They mourned over him, saying, “Alas, my brother!”
medium.q: How did the old prophet and his sons express their grief?

answers: He believed the prophecy concerning the altar and high places would come to pass
They were members of the same family
It was the only grave in the city
medium.explanation: His request showed that he believed the word spoken against the altar and high places would be fulfilled.
medium.q: Why did the old prophet want to be buried beside the man of God?

medium.explanation: To mourn means to grieve and express sorrow over someone who has died.
medium.q: What does “mourn” mean in this passage?

answers: He believed that the prophecy would come to pass
He had never heard the prophecy
challenge.explanation: His request to be buried beside the man of God was based on his belief that the prophecy would be fulfilled.
challenge.q: What did the old prophet's burial request reveal about his attitude toward the prophecy?

answers: The burial had no connection with the prophecy
He connected his future burial with the fulfillment of the prophecy against the altar and high places
The burial caused the altar to be rent
challenge.explanation: He wanted his bones beside the man of God because he believed the prophecy against the altar and high places.
challenge.q: What connection did the old prophet make between the burial and the prophecy?

answers: He showed grief and respect toward him
He appointed him as a priest
challenge.explanation: He carried the body, mourned over it, and buried it in his own grave, showing grief and respect.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the old prophet personally burying the man of God?

paragraphs.title: Jeroboam Does Not Turn from His Evil Way

easy.explanation: The passage says that Jeroboam returned not from his evil way.
easy.q: Did Jeroboam turn from his evil way after these events?

easy.explanation: Jeroboam continued making priests of the high places.
easy.q: Whom did Jeroboam continue to make priests?

answers: It was cut off and destroyed
easy.explanation: The sin would cut off and destroy the house of Jeroboam.
easy.q: What was the result of the sin of the house of Jeroboam?

answers: Only from the men of Judah
medium.explanation: The passage says that whosoever would, Jeroboam consecrated as a priest.
medium.q: From whom did Jeroboam make priests of the high places?

answers: It became the sin of the house of Jeroboam
It became the great honor of the house
It had no connection with the house of Jeroboam
medium.explanation: The appointment of these priests became sin unto the house of Jeroboam.
medium.q: What was the significance of the high-place priesthood for Jeroboam's house?

answers: To remove or destroy it completely
medium.explanation: In this context, “to cut it off” means to remove or destroy the house completely.
medium.q: What does “to cut it off” mean in this context?

answers: The signs and miracle did not cause him to leave his evil way
The sign caused him to abolish the high places
The prophecy was never delivered to Jeroboam
challenge.explanation: Despite the prophecy, sign, and miracle, Jeroboam continued in his evil way.
challenge.q: What was the central contrast between the earlier events and Jeroboam's response?

answers: It was part of the sin that brought judgment upon the house
It was intended to correct the worship at the high places
challenge.explanation: The continued appointment of these priests was identified as the sin that brought destruction upon the house.
challenge.q: How was the appointment of priests of the high places related to the sin of Jeroboam's house?

answers: The position was open to anyone who wanted it
The position was limited to a fixed royal lineage
No one was allowed to become a priest
challenge.explanation: The wording shows that Jeroboam appointed anyone who desired the position.
challenge.q: What does “whosoever would, he consecrated him” reveal about the appointment of priests?
